text:
maria_p: Quick sync request from a pilot customer. They want per-response traceable IDs and token accounting in the response so their analytics and billing pipelines don't need console queries.

sanjay_api: We can surface that but must keep it stable and small. Recommend `meta.trace_id` (public), `meta.request_id` (id per HTTP request), and a compact `usage` object. Avoid internal hostnames.

kai_ml: Important: token counts must match the served model's tokenizer. Add `tokenizer_id` (e.g., "r/rwkv-v1.tok-v2") so customers can reconcile on replay. Also call out that token counts are ints (no floats) and represent model-consumed tokens.

ellie_cs: From support: customers will expect same fields across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. If fields differ, we need clear docs and a deprecation/opt-in plan. Enterprise customers may want `billing_cost_usd` inline.

maria_p: Proposed GA surface (minimal): `meta.trace_id`, `meta.request_id`, `usage.input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens`, `usage.total_tokens`. Extended (enterprise opt-in): `meta.route_hint`, `deployment_info`, `billing_cost_usd`, `tokenizer_id`.

sanjay_api: API shape idea: put metadata at top-level to avoid interfering with `choices`/`data`. Example payload we can show in docs: 

```json
{
  "meta": {"trace_id":"r-4f3a2b","request_id":"req-20260321-1","fallback_to":[]},
  "usage": {"input_tokens":24,"output_tokens":76,"total_tokens":100},
  "response": {"choices":[{"text":"Hello"}]}
}
```

kai_ml: For embeddings/rerank: include `usage.unit` e.g., "tokens" vs "embedding_units" and a `usage.unit_cost` optional field when `billing_cost_usd` is present.

ellie_cs: Launch checklist suggestion: 1) SDKs (py/js) map these fields and don't break existing parsers, 2) Docs include example for fallback scenario and multi-model rollouts, 3) Privacy sign-off for route hints and deployment_info, 4) Opt-out mechanism for inline costs.

maria_p: Rollout plan: GA minimal for Hosted (enabled by default), extended fields behind enterprise feature flag and enabled on Dedicated/Private by default (but documented). Keep `meta.trace_id` length limit (128 chars) and canonical prefix `r-`.

sanjay_api: Implementation note: router will stamp `trace_id` once at ingress. Keep it stable across retries and fallbacks. If a fallback happens we keep same `trace_id` and append fallback details to `meta.fallback_to`.

kai_ml: I'll add `meta.tokenizer_id` to model responses and include tokenizer version. Also will add a short paragraph about tokenization caveats (prompt truncation, system messages counted differently).

ellie_cs: Customer comms: include sample curl/python/js showing correlation of `trace_id` to console logs and billing export. Devex will prep snippets.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch feature/response-meta (sha: b7d9f0) :rocket:

maria_p: Action items: @sanjay_api open PR with schema, feature-flag toggle and migration notes; @kai_ml add tokenizer_id and token-count tests; @ellie_cs draft launch comms and support playbook. Review in Thursday sync.

sanjay_api: Quick question: should `trace_id` be stable if client retries after network failure? I vote yes (same logical request).

maria_p: Agreed. Use same `trace_id` for client retries; if the request triggers a different logical flow (explicit user retry after failure) return a new `trace_id`.

kai_ml: I'll prototype a fallback metadata example too: \"meta\": {\"trace_id\":\"r-4f3a2b\",\"fallback_to\":[{\"model\":\"gpt-3.5-x\",\"route\":\"dedicated-v2\"}]}

ellie_cs: 44d thanks, looks good. This should reduce support tickets where customers ask \"why did my tokens/billing mismatch?\"

maria_p: Last note: keep response surface minimal at GA; we can iterate once cost math and SDKs are stable.

(End of thread)
